title: Feed and Schema
summary: Register market families, ingest deterministic trade and quote rows, and query them back in the same structure a trading team would expect.
whySQLiteFallsShort: SQLite can store rows, but it does not give a trading team a first-class market-data contract with schema-aware ingest and revision labels built into the engine surface.
SydraDB makes the write path explicit: a feed handler can register a market family, post NDJSON rows, and query them back without inventing a separate row-to-timeseries fanout layer.
The same engine that stores the rows is the one later used for grouped analysis and storage-aware correction workflows.
